items.s: Our school has turned its flat roof ___ a garden.
items.tip: turn A into B = change A so it becomes B.
items.say: Our school has turned its flat roof into a garden.
items.ask: Our school has turned its flat roof blank a garden.

items.s: The idea came from Ms Ortiz, ___ class wanted somewhere to grow vegetables.
items.tip: whose = belonging to the person before it: Ms Ortiz's class → whose class.
items.say: The idea came from Ms Ortiz, whose class wanted somewhere to grow vegetables.
items.ask: The idea came from Ms Ortiz, blank class wanted somewhere to grow vegetables.

items.s: ___ the strong winds up there, almost everything has grown well.
items.tip: Despite + a noun (the winds) = even though there are strong winds. (No 'of' after despite!)
items.say: Despite the strong winds up there, almost everything has grown well.
items.ask: Blank the strong winds up there, almost everything has grown well.

items.s: There are now ___ many tomatoes that the canteen uses them in lunches.
items.tip: so + many/much + that: so many tomatoes that… (such goes with a noun: such a success).
items.say: There are now so many tomatoes that the canteen uses them in lunches.
items.ask: There are now blank many tomatoes that the canteen uses them in lunches.

items.s: The bees, ___ live in two hives by the door, love the lavender.
items.tip: which for things and animals after a comma (not that).
items.say: The bees, which live in two hives by the door, love the lavender.
items.ask: The bees, blank live in two hives by the door, love the lavender.

items.s: Pupils aren't allowed on the roof ___ a teacher is with them.
items.tip: unless = except if: not allowed unless a teacher is there.
items.say: Pupils aren't allowed on the roof unless a teacher is with them.
items.ask: Pupils aren't allowed on the roof blank a teacher is with them.

items.s: It has been ___ a success that other schools have come to visit.
items.tip: such + a + noun + that: such a success that… (so + adjective: so successful that…).
items.say: It has been such a success that other schools have come to visit.
items.ask: It has been blank a success that other schools have come to visit.

items.s: Next spring, we hope to set ___ a stall selling honey to parents.
items.tip: set up = start or build something (a stall, a club).
items.say: Next spring, we hope to set up a stall selling honey to parents.
items.ask: Next spring, we hope to set blank a stall selling honey to parents.

books.name: Making Our Own Film
books.focus: none of · had known · than · as · all

items.s: When our drama teacher suggested making a film, none ___ us knew how hard it would be.
items.tip: none of + us/them/the… = not one person in the group.
items.say: When our drama teacher suggested making a film, none of us knew how hard it would be.
items.ask: When our drama teacher suggested making a film, none blank us knew how hard it would be.

items.s: We spent weeks writing the script, ___ turned out to be the easy part.
items.tip: which after a comma can point back to a whole idea (writing the script).
items.say: We spent weeks writing the script, which turned out to be the easy part.
items.ask: We spent weeks writing the script, blank turned out to be the easy part.

items.s: Filming outdoors was tricky, ___ it rained almost every day.
items.tip: as = because, giving the reason.
items.say: Filming outdoors was tricky, as it rained almost every day.
items.ask: Filming outdoors was tricky, blank it rained almost every day.

items.s: Jake, ___ played the hero, kept forgetting his lines.
items.tip: who for people, between commas for extra information.
items.say: Jake, who played the hero, kept forgetting his lines.
items.ask: Jake, blank played the hero, kept forgetting his lines.

items.s: If we ___ known how long editing takes, we would have started earlier.
items.tip: Third conditional: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle (about the past).
items.say: If we had known how long editing takes, we would have started earlier.
items.ask: If we blank known how long editing takes, we would have started earlier.

items.s: In the end, it took ___ three months to finish.
items.tip: it takes/took + person + time: it took us three months. (almost, nearly or about fit too.)
items.say: In the end, it took us three months to finish.
items.ask: In the end, it took blank three months to finish.

items.s: On premiere night, there were more people ___ seats in the hall.
items.tip: more … than compares two amounts.
items.say: On premiere night, there were more people than seats in the hall.
items.ask: On premiere night, there were more people blank seats in the hall.

items.s: Everyone agreed it had been worth ___ the hard work.
items.tip: worth all the work = every bit of it was worth it.
items.say: Everyone agreed it had been worth all the hard work.
items.ask: Everyone agreed it had been worth blank the hard work.

books.name: The Night Walk
books.focus: set off · anything · neither … nor · until · could

items.s: Last autumn, our scout group went ___ a night walk through the woods.
items.tip: go on a walk / go for a walk: both are right.
items.say: Last autumn, our scout group went on a night walk through the woods.
items.ask: Last autumn, our scout group went blank a night walk through the woods.

items.s: We set ___ long after dark, which felt very strange.
items.tip: set off / set out = start a journey.
items.say: We set off long after dark, which felt very strange.
items.ask: We set blank long after dark, which felt very strange.

items.s: At first, I could hardly see ___ at all.
items.tip: hardly is almost a 'not', so we use anything (not something, not nothing).
items.say: At first, I could hardly see anything at all.
items.ask: At first, I could hardly see blank at all.

items.s: ___ my best friend nor I had ever heard a real owl before.
items.tip: Neither A nor B = not A and not B.
items.say: Neither my best friend nor I had ever heard a real owl before.
items.ask: Blank my best friend nor I had ever heard a real owl before.

items.s: Then, all of a sudden, one hooted right ___ our heads.
items.tip: above / over = higher than: right above our heads.
items.say: Then, all of a sudden, one hooted right above our heads.
items.ask: Then, all of a sudden, one hooted right blank our heads.

items.s: We stood completely still ___ it flew away.
items.tip: until = up to the moment that something happens.
items.say: We stood completely still until it flew away.
items.ask: We stood completely still blank it flew away.

items.s: I'd never have guessed that the woods ___ be so full of life at night.
items.tip: could = was possible (the past of can).
items.say: I'd never have guessed that the woods could be so full of life at night.
items.ask: I'd never have guessed that the woods blank be so full of life at night.

items.s: It's a night I'll remember for the rest ___ my life.
items.tip: the rest of = all the remaining part: the rest of my life.
items.say: It's a night I'll remember for the rest of my life.
items.ask: It's a night I'll remember for the rest blank my life.
